capabilities.description: List a page of child folders, or search them by name. The default is the first page of folders at the project root.
Get an asset folder by ID
Create an asset folder with an optional parent folder ID
Rename an asset folder
Delete an empty asset folder by ID

Move a folder under another folder, or to the project root. Needs the Manage project permission (project:manage), which administrators hold, because moving a folder changes who can access everything inside it.

Upload a new asset to a project. Images up to 10 MiB, audio and video up to 50 MiB and 120 seconds, and other files up to 5,000 MiB can be sent in one request. Images up to 20 MiB, and any file within its limit, can also be sent in sequential parts with a multipart upload, which can resume after a failed part; CalmLens accumulates parts and enforces the final total, and checks `totalSizeInBytes` up front when you send it. Retained multipart image originals are served through CalmLens CDN URLs. Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to retry safely without creating a second asset.

Upload a sequential part for an in-progress asset upload. Each non-final part must be at least 5 MiB, an upload has at most 10,000 parts, and image uploads in parts must total at most 20 MiB. The final part uses the `wait` choice saved when the upload started unless you pass `wait` here. To stream raw bytes instead of JSON, send the `X-CalmLens-Upload: part` header and pass `partNumber`, `isFinal` and `sizeInBytes` as query parameters.
List a page of the project's assets, optionally in one folder or matching a filter

Search accessible assets by keyword or natural language. Images are indexed automatically; enable audio and video search in project settings to include those media types. Results are the best `pageSize` matches (at most 20), ranked by relevance, so this endpoint has no cursor: refine the query, or list assets with a filter, to see more.
Get a single asset by ID
Get child assets of a parent asset

Page through every segment of an audio or video asset's findings timeline, in time order. The asset's `classification.moderation.timeline.segmentCount` says how many there are. Lists nothing for other assets or while a copyright hold is on, and returns `asset/held` while a safety hold is on
Update an existing asset
Remove stored content, including the content derived from it in child assets, while retaining the asset records
Delete an uploaded asset, its child assets and their stored content from a project. Child assets (those with a `parentId`) are deleted only with the asset they were extracted from.
Move an asset into a folder, or to the project root

Process an asset whose `classification.status` is `failed` again. It returns to `processing` and is moderated like a new upload. The moderation decision must still be pending and the asset must not be under a safety hold. Processing needs available file content, inline text, or an eligible website URL to load again.

Complete the policy evidence behind an asset's moderation decision. To decide quickly, moderation skips questions whose answers could not change any action, so a report marked `moderation.explanationComplete: false` can credit a different rule, or show a different policy score, than a complete report would. Explaining answers those questions for the same content and returns the asset with `moderation.explanationComplete: true`; every action stays as decided. A decision made under policy settings that have since changed can't be explained as made: re-run it with `rerun: true` instead.

Record a reviewer's decision on an asset, replacing the policy's. The asset's `classification.moderation.status` becomes the decision, the matching `asset.<status>` event is sent with the request's `actor` (the API key, or the person an assistant's key acts for), and the decision and note are added to its review history. An asset still pending moderation can only be blocked or purged. Purging also needs `assets:delete` and permanently deletes the stored content.

Delete up to 500 assets, or remove their stored content, in one request. Every asset must exist in the project, the API key needs `assets:delete` for its folder, and `delete` takes only uploaded assets, not child assets (those with a `parentId`); otherwise nothing is queued. The response gives the operation's `batchId` and confirms that it is queued. It then runs in the background: `delete` deletes each asset with its child assets and stored content and records `asset.deleted`, and `remove-content` removes the content as a removal would (reason `requested`) and records `asset.content-removed`; each of those events carries the `batch-id` fact. Assets under a safety hold, or in a folder the key can no longer delete from when the operation runs, are skipped and record no event. To follow the operation, read the events feed filtered by those types or by asset.
Create a short-lived signed URL for a private asset, the base URL of all its CDN resources
Create each lens, or change it to the definition sent, by identifier. An unchanged lens is returned as it is, so applications can send their lenses every time they start.
List a page of the project's lenses, newest first. The built-in lenses are always available and aren't listed.
Create a lens. Its identifier must be new to the project.
Get one of the project's lenses by ID
Change a lens's name, description, type, transform or whether the CDN serves it. The CDN serves the new transform from then on.
Delete a lens. URLs that select it stop being served; files the CDN already delivered may stay in caches until they expire.

List project events, oldest first, after a cursor. Webhook connectors deliver each event in the same shape. Each event's `facts` are `{ key, value, url? }` entries registered for its `type` (see the event types in the webhooks guide). Omit `cursor` to get a cursor for the current time without any events, then pass each response's `nextCursor` as `cursor`. When `hasMore` is false you have caught up; keep the cursor to poll for later events. Filter by `types` or `assetId` to receive only some events; a cursor belongs to its filters, and one used with other filters returns `cursor/invalid`. Polling receives new events without a public webhook URL, for example during local development.
Get a page of a project's hash lists, newest first
Get a hash list by ID
Create a hash list. Image uploads are compared with every list in the project: a `flag` list reports matches, a `block` list also blocks close matches.
Rename a hash list or change what its matches do. The new action applies to later uploads.
Delete a hash list and every entry in it. Later uploads are no longer compared with it.
Get a page of the hashes in a hash list, newest first
Add a PDQ hash to a hash list, either as a hash or from an image asset. Adding a hash the list already holds returns the existing entry.
Remove a hash from its hash list. Later uploads no longer match it.
List a page of the moderation policies of the API key's organisation, oldest first. Policies are shared by the organisation's projects; Get Project Policy says which one a project uses.
Get one of the organisation's moderation policies by ID
Create a moderation policy in the API key's organisation, from settings or as a copy of a built-in preset. It moderates nothing until you assign it to a project or name it on an upload preset.

Change a policy's name, description or settings. Changes apply to later moderation. Saving a `live` policy pins it as a copy under the same ID. Only policies that no other project uses can be changed through a project's key.
Restore the settings of the preset release a `pinned` or `copy` policy is pinned to, discarding its edits
Move a `pinned` or `copy` policy whose settings are unchanged from its preset release to the latest release of the preset

Switch automatic updates on or off for one of the organisation's own preset policies: on turns a `pinned` policy `live`, so it always has the latest preset settings, and off pins a `live` policy at its current preset release.
Delete a policy that no project or upload preset uses. Only policies that no other project uses can be deleted through a project's key.
Get the policy the project moderates with. Uploads through an upload preset that names its own policy use that one instead.
Choose the policy the project moderates with. Later uploads use it, except those through an upload preset that names its own policy.

defaults.description: Deadline of each API request attempt, including reading the response body. cdn.serve's ends when the response headers arrive. Text uploads use it too.
Deadline of each binary upload attempt (file content and multipart parts): none unless set.

Retries after a retryable failure (surface.json retryable), for GET and HEAD requests and requests that carry an Idempotency-Key, unless their body is a one-shot stream. Each retry reuses the Idempotency-Key.
observedBy: the client retries twice by default, then raises the last error

defaults.description: Backoff before retry n (0-based): d = min(retryMaxDelayMs, retryBaseDelayMs * 2^n); the client waits d/2 + random * d/2, rounded. A Retry-After header (seconds or an HTTP date; 0 retries at once) replaces the backoff.
observedBy: 502 and 504 are retried with exponential backoff and jitter

defaults.description: The longest backoff before a retry.
A Retry-After longer than this is not waited out: the error (or, for cdn.serve, the response) goes back to the caller.
observedBy: a Retry-After over 60 seconds is returned to the caller without retrying
